summary: The Appellant - a High Tension consumer in the State of Maharashtra has, in this Appeal, assailed order dated 12.07.2021 passed by the 3[rd] Respondent - Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission (hereinafter referred to as “MERC/Commission”) whereby the petition filed by the Appellant bearing No. 17 of 2021 has been dismissed. The prayers made in the petition by the Appellant are quoted herein below: - _b) That this Hon’ble Commission be pleased to declare that the Respondent has wrongly denied the Petitioner the various incentives by wrongly treating the Petitioner to be in arrears;_ _c) That this Hon’ble Commission be pleased to declare that the Petitioner is entitled to refund of an amount of Rs. 10,36,76,259/(Rs. Ten Crore thirty six lakh seventy six thousand and two hundred fifty nine only) as per the tabular statement annexed as_ _**Exhibit N** hereto and direct the Respondents to pay the same to the Petitioner including interest thereon at the rate of 18% p.a. from the date of the filing of this Petition till realization;_ _e) That this Hon’ble Commission be pleased to direct the Respondents to pay to the Petitioner a sum of Rs. 5,00,000/towards legal expenses incurred by the Petitioner in connection with this Petition;_ particularly with regard to take or pay provisions for 25% of power requirement and restriction on reduction in contract demand. Upon analysis of the contentions of the parties in that petition, following three issues were framed by Commission for its consideration:- The Commission vide its order dated 21.05.2004 allowed the petition and decided all the three issues in favour of the Appellant. This order of the Commission was assailed by MSEDCL before this Tribunal by way of Appeal No. 29 of 2007 which came to be dismissed vide judgment dated 30.05.2007. Para Nos. 19 and 21 of the said judgment of this Tribunal are material and are extracted herein below:- This Tribunal, thus, upheld the findings/observations/directions of the Commission contained in the order dated 21.05.2004. Ultimately this Tribunal held in para Nos. 27 and 28 of the said judgment as under:- Aggrieved by the said judgment of this Tribunal, the MSEDCL approached the Hon’ble Supreme Court by way of Civil Appeal No. 4304 of 2007 which has been allowed vide judgment dated 28.02.2020. The Supreme Court set aside the orders passed by the Commission as well as this Tribunal and held that circulars and the policy decisions issued before the establishment of the Commission were illegally quashed. Accordingly, the order concerning refund of amount recovered by MSEB also was set aside. Perusal of the impugned order of the Commission would reveal that the Commission found that the prayers made in the petition by the Appellant as well as the contentions raised therein have already been decided in the first round of litigation commencing from filing of petition No. 35 of 2002 before the Commission and culminating in passing of the judgment dated 28.02.2020 by the Hon’ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal No. 4304 and accordingly dismissed the petition. It is argued by the Learned Senior Counsel for the Appellant that in the judgment dated 28.02.2020, the Hon’ble Supreme Court was mainly concerned about the various circulars issued by the MSEDCL and on finding those circulars legal as well as valid and holding that the Commission had no power to quash those circulars, the Apex Court allowed the Civil Appeal. It is his submission that the other two issues namely reduction contract demand and extension of supply from CPP to Unit E-1 raised by the Appellant in the previous petition before the Commission have been left untouched by the Hon’ble Supreme Court and therefore the previous order of the Commission dated 21.05.2004 in petition No. 35 of 2002 as upheld by this Tribunal in Appeal No. 29 of 2007 hold the field and are applicable in this regard and therefore the Appellant is entitled to the amounts from MSEDCL as sought for in the instant petition which was filed before the Commission. Learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the 1[st] Respondent-MSEDCL has refuted the submission of the Learned Senior Counsel for the Appellant saying that the parties had raised all these contentions in the Civil Appeal before the Hon’ble Supreme Court which were duly considered and since the Appeal has been allowed, it cannot be said that any issue has been left undecided by the Apex Court. its challenge to the judgment of this Tribunal in Appeal No. 29 of 2007 to any particular aspect. In fact, it is evident that MSEDCL had assailed each and every finding given by the Commission in order dated 21.05.2004, as upheld by this Tribunal in judgment dated 30.05.2007 in Appeal No. 29 of 2007. Para 7 and 8 of the grounds raised in the Civil Appeal before the Hon’ble Supreme Court are also relevant in this regard and are extracted herein below:- _“7. Because the Appellate Tribunal failed to appreciate that so far as the case of respondent No. 3 is concerned, Govt. of India issues a letter dated 22.8.1994 clearly contemplating both the units of respondent No.3 as separate units and as such the Tribunal erred in holding that there is no power vested in the appellant to refuse reduction of the contract demand._ In view of the same, we are of the opinion that the petition filed by the Appellant before the Commission was totally misconceived and a malafide attempt to obtain what was devised to it by the Supreme Court in judgment dated 28.02.2020 in the first round of litigation and therefore was rightly dismissed by the Commission. Having regard to these facts and circumstances of the instant case and the manner in which the instant petition has been filed claiming the reliefs identical to that which had been claimed in the earlier litigation and negated by the Hon’ble Supreme Court in judgment dated 28.02.2020, we do not find any error or infirmity in the impugned order of the Commission. The appeal is found sans any merit and is, accordingly, dismissed.
title: EUROTEX INDUSTRIES AND EXPORTS LIMITED VERSUS MAHARASHTRA STATE ELECTRICITY DISTRIBUTION COMPANY LTD. & Anr
